permutationLabel: ASGE 2019 intermediate risk (age >55, abnormal LFTs, CBD 7 mm, no stone seen) → MRCP/EUS or IOC, not ERCP
summary: 62-year-old man with two biliary episodes this week, now pain-free and not jaundiced; bilirubin 30 µmol/L (1.75 mg/dL), ALT 140, ALP 190; ultrasound shows gallstones and a 7 mm CBD without a visible stone.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Two episodes of right upper abdominal pain this week
inputs.hpi: Two episodes of severe right upper quadrant pain this week, each lasting about 4 hours, the second with dark urine for a day. Now pain-free. No fever, no visible jaundice, stools normal.

exam.abdomen: Soft, minimal right upper quadrant tenderness.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Gallstones in a normal-walled gallbladder. CBD 7 mm; the distal duct is obscured by bowel gas and no duct stone is seen. No intrahepatic duct dilatation.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected choledocholithiasis — ASGE intermediate risk
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Symptomatic gallstones with suspected choledocholithiasis — ASGE 2019 intermediate risk (age >55, abnormal liver tests, CBD 7 mm, no stone seen). For MRCP or EUS before cholecystectomy.

recommended.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): asge-cbd not recommended; recommended: tg18-cholangitis, tg18-cholecystitis, qsofa, sofa, news2, mews

mustInclude.note: ASGE intermediate risk: EUS or MRCP (or intra-operative cholangiography/laparoscopic US) to confirm a duct stone before any ERCP.

mustExclude.note: ASGE 2019 (intermediate risk): do not proceed straight to ERCP — about half of these patients have no stone, and ERCP carries a 3–10% risk of post-ERCP pancreatitis, bleeding and perforation. An unconditional ERCP line in the plan is a patient-safety defect.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Choledocholithiasis protocol and dx-variants: add ASGE 2019 risk variants (high → ERCP; intermediate → EUS/MRCP or IOC/LCBDE, ERCP only if a stone is confirmed; low → LC ± IOC), fed by the existing asgeCbd scale.

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: ASGE guideline on the role of endoscopy in the evaluation and management of choledocholithiasis
guideline.section: Risk strata. High: CBD stone on US/cross-sectional imaging, or total bilirubin >4 mg/dL with dilated CBD, or ascending cholangitis → ERCP. Intermediate: abnormal liver tests, age >55, or dilated CBD → EUS/MRCP or intra-operative cholangiography/laparoscopic US. Low: none → cholecystectomy without further CBD evaluation
guideline.citation: Buxbaum JL, Abbas Fehmi SM, Sultan S, et al. Gastrointest Endosc. 2019;89:1075–1105.e15.

guideline.name: BSG updated guideline on the management of common bile duct stones
guideline.section: MRCP/EUS when CBDS suspected but not confirmed; cholecystectomy after ERCP clearance (within 2 weeks) unless unfit
guideline.citation: Williams E, Beckingham I, El Sayed G, et al. Gut. 2017;66:765–782.

guideline.name: NICE CG188 — Gallstone disease: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Asymptomatic gallbladder stones in a normal gallbladder and biliary tree: reassure, no treatment; symptomatic gallbladder stones: offer laparoscopic cholecystectomy; LFTs and ultrasound for suspected gallstone disease
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG188, October 2014.

rationale: Permutation: ASGE intermediate risk. The distinguishing guideline decision is to image the duct (MRCP/EUS or IOC) rather than go straight to ERCP. Tests whether the plan adapts to the risk stratum.
